newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa shares push higher after H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Endesa shares push higher after H1 results.

text.p: Shares in Spanish electricity group Endesa pushed higher on Wednesday, outperforming the market after the utility announced its first half results.
At 1300 GMT the shares were up 3.03 percent to 3,235 pesetas, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares had risen 1.61 percent at 6,804.80.
The utility said first half net profit had fallen 3.9 percent to 78.59 billion pesetas.
Despite the fall, dealers said the market was satisfied since the drop in earnings had been the result of a one-off restatement of assets and results had improved versus the first quarter.
"There has been a one-off high depreciation charge, but the company will get that back in tax benefits in the next few years," said one dealer at a foreign brokerage.
"The underlying results were not out of line, in fact they were better than expected," he added.
Endesa said it had increased its writedowns by 15.85 billion pesetas to 53.07 billion.

A change in the law last year allows companies to update the value of fixed assets in return for tax benefits. Utilities and property companies are hardest hit due to their high proportion of fixed assets.
"At this rate the end year results will be slightly ahead of last year, despite this charge," said one dealer.
Endesa reported a fall in quarter one net profit to 39.21 billion pesetas from 42.64 billion.
